assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental realisation of Hubbard-type many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition and single-site quantum gas microscopy, gave a controllable platform for statistical and many-body problems. The impact on condensed-matter theory, quantum simulation and cold-atom physics is broad and original.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) supplied the theoretical proposals; Bloch and Greiner made decisive experimental realisations. Esslinger has strong claims through fermionic lattices and cannot be included within a three-person limit, so the credit boundary is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation across many groups; the interpretation of the Mott transition and lattice simulation is stable. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Choosing three of Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger is contentious.
Overlap with the quantum computing and simulation candidate (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) complicates how a prize would be framed.
I rely on my own recollection of the history and have not verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators routine, enabling dispersive readout, gate operations and the leading architecture for quantum processors. The concept is clear, original and has had very large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling experimentally in 2004; Girvin, Blais and Schoelkopf wrote the theoretical proposal. A three-person prize is possible but excludes Blais, and my recollection is that a recent prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits may affect how the field is weighed.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and now scientifically and commercially central; confirmation is strong and independent. Timing is good, though recent circuit-related recognition may argue for a pause.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a separate discovery from circuit quantum mechanics already honoured.
Exclusion of Blais or others from the proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a paradigm of non-equilibrium statistical physics, defining a universality class for stochastic growth with exact solutions linked to random matrix theory. The depth, the connection to random matrices and the relevance across systems are compelling from my own field perspective.
assessment.attribution: The original theory is credited to Kardar, Parisi and Zhang; the supplied credit omits Parisi, which is a fairness problem (he received a prize in 2021, which may matter). Takeuchi provided the clearest experimental confirmation, in liquid-crystal turbulence, including Tracy-Widom statistics.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986, with exact solutions and clean experimental verification in the 2010s. Mature, with a well-understood interpretation.
uncertainties: Absence of Parisi among the credited names complicates attribution.
Experimental confirmation of the full universality class is limited to a few systems.
Whether the committee prefers theory or experiment as the central contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum materials, a rich platform for strongly correlated electrons with many follow-on discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators observed the correlated states. This is a natural theory plus experiment pairing, though other experimentalists contributed to the picture.
assessment.maturity: Observations are reproduced by many groups, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated phases is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Many experimental contributors lie outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model and was a landmark in particle physics. The importance is beyond doubt, though the theoretical recognition came in 2013.
assessment.attribution: ATLAS and CMS are collaborations of thousands; Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee led the proposals and construction, which fits a pattern of recognising instrument leadership. The allocation is inherently arbitrary and others could be argued for.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, confirmed by two independent experiments and subsequent precision measurements.
uncertainties: Whether collaboration leadership is a suitable basis for a prize configuration.
The 2013 prize already honoured the theory, which may weaken the case for further recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unified the rigidity of grains, foams and glasses via a critical point with scaling and a statistical description. It is conceptually close to my interests in disordered systems and has had broad influence on soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram in 1998; the pairing is natural, though O'Hern, Silbert and Witten are important for the point-J picture and are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Well developed with simulations and experiments, but the connection to real glasses and the universality of the critical behaviour are still debated.
uncertainties: Universality and the status of point J in finite dimensions are unresolved.
Relation to the glass transition remains controversial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength concept, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. The invention is original and has transformed precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye demonstrated extreme performance; a two-person configuration is plausible, though frequency combs were already honoured in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Mature in performance and reproduced by many groups; a redefinition of the second is anticipated but not yet done, so recognition could be timed to that.
uncertainties: Whether other groups also deserve credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a major branch of condensed matter physics built on topology.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory and Molenkamp the first experimental observation; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe case and are not in the credited names, and 3D topological insulator work adds further credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many materials, including three-dimensional topological insulators; the interpretation is stable. Timing is acceptable, but the topology theme was recognised in 2016.
uncertainties: Absence of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the credited names weakens fairness.
Closeness to the 2016 prize on topological phases.
